inputs.original_text: DHS is using a baby’s medical emergency in a crowded TSA line at JFK to manufacture an ICE hero narrative. They control the footage, so what they’re showing is a polished version designed to steer public opinion—not proof that we’ve seen the whole story. This looks like image management dressed up as transparency.
inputs.modified_text: DHS is turning a baby’s medical emergency in a crowded TSA line at JFK into a carefully managed ICE publicity operation. They control the footage, which means the public is being shown only what serves the hero narrative—not necessarily the full story. Calling it transparency doesn’t change the basic trick: manage the images, shape the reaction, and bury the questions.
